'''Władysław Minor''' also known as '''Wladek Minor''' (born 1946) is a Polish-American [[biophysicist]], a specialist in [[structural biology]] and [[protein crystallography]]. He is a Harrison Distinguished Professor of Molecular Physiology and Biological Physics at the [[University of Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://med.virginia.edu/faculty/faculty-listing/wm4n/|title=Minor, Wladek}}</ref> Minor is a co-author of  HKL2000/HKL3000 – crystallographic data processing and structure solution software used to process data and solve structures of macromolecules, as well as small molecules.<ref name="auto1">{{cite book |doi=10.1016/S0076-6879(97)76066-X |chapter=Processing of X-ray diffraction data collected in oscillation mode |title=Macromolecular Crystallography Part A |series=Methods in Enzymology |year=1997 |last1=Otwinowski |first1=Zbyszek |last2=Minor |first2=Wladek |volume=276 |pages=307–326 |pmid=27799103 |isbn=978-0-12-182177-7 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Minor |first1=Wladek |last2=Cymborowski |first2=Marcin |last3=Otwinowski |first3=Zbyszek |last4=Chruszcz |first4=Maksymilian |title=HKL -3000: the integration of data reduction and structure solution – from diffraction images to an initial model in minutes |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section D: Biological Crystallography |date=1 August 2006 |volume=62 |issue=8 |pages=859–866 |doi=10.1107/S0907444906019949 |pmid=16855301 |bibcode=2006AcCrD..62..859M |doi-access=free }}</ref> He is a co-founder of HKL Research, a company that distributes the software.  He is also a co-author of a public repository of diffraction images (proteindiffraction.org) for some of the protein structures available in the [[Protein Data Bank]] and other software tools for structural biology.

== Early life and education ==
Władysław Minor was born in Poland in May 1946. He obtained his M.Sc. degree in 1969 (supervisor - Bronisław Buras) and his Ph.D. degree in 1977 (supervisor - Izabela Sosnowska) from the Physics Department at the [[University of Warsaw]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite journal |last1=Jaskolski |first1=Mariusz |last2=Wlodawer |first2=Alexander |last3=Dauter |first3=Zbigniew |last4=Shabalin |first4=Ivan |last5=Chruszcz |first5=Maksymilian |title=Celebrating the 75th birthday of Professor Wladek Minor, one of the most accomplished Polish-American structural biologists |journal=Acta Biochimica Polonica |date=21 January 2021 |volume=68 |issue=1 |pages=1–4 |doi=10.18388/abp.2020_5539 |pmid=33476109 |doi-access=free }}</ref> He moved to the United States in 1985 at the age of 39.<ref name="auto2" />

== Career and research ==
Minor's main focus of interest during the Ph.D. studies was [[solid-state physics]]. For several years after receiving his Ph.D. from the [[University of Warsaw]], he continued to work in this area of research.

After moving to the United States in 1985 and working with [[Michael Rossmann]]  at  [[Purdue University]], he gradually switched into the field of macromolecular crystallography.<ref name="auto2" /> While at Purdue, Minor started a collaboration with {{ill|Zbyszek Otwinowski|pl|Zbyszek Otwinowski|display=1}}, with whom they developed software for processing X-ray diffraction data (Denzo, Scalepack, XDisplayF). Their paper “Processing of X-ray diffraction data collected in oscillation mode” published in 1997 <ref name="auto1" /> was listed as number 23 in the list of 100 most-cited research papers of all times.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Van Noorden |first1=Richard |last2=Maher |first2=Brendan |last3=Nuzzo |first3=Regina |title=The top 100 papers |journal=Nature |date=30 October 2014 |volume=514 |issue=7524 |pages=550–553 |doi=10.1038/514550a |pmid=25355343 |bibcode=2014Natur.514..550V |s2cid=4466906 |doi-access=free }}</ref>  As of 2021, this paper has been cited over 41000 times (according to [[Google Scholar]]).<ref name="googlescholar">{{Google Scholar id | 5zjVsfQAAAAJ| Wladek Minor}})</ref>

In  1995,  Minor joined the [[University of Virginia]] as a faculty member. Around the same time, he and Zbyszek Otwinowski founded HKL Research.

Starting from 2000,  his lab was a part of two [[Protein Structure Initiative]] centers: the Midwest Center for Structural Genomic (MSCG)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anl.gov/bio/midwest-center-for-structural-genomics|title=Midwest Center for Structural Genomics &#124; Argonne National Laboratory|website=www.anl.gov}}</ref> and the New York [[Structural genomics|Structural Genomics]] Research Consortium (NYSGRC).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nysgxrc.org/psi3-cgi/index.cgi|title=NYSGRC|website=www.nysgxrc.org}}</ref>  The lab was also a part of the Center for Structural Genomics of Infectious Diseases (CSGID)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://csgid.org/|title=Center for Structural Genomics of Infectious Diseases|website=csgid.org}}</ref> and the [[Enzyme Function Initiative]]. The Minor lab developed and maintained [[data management]] and structure solution tools, as well as performed quality control of the crystal structures and conducted determination of some of the structures.<ref name="auto2" />

The Minor lab has developed many other software tools for structural biology, including proteindiffraction.org (a public repository of diffraction images),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Grabowski == Personal life ==
Wladek Minor is married to Iwona Minor. They have two sons.<ref name="auto2" />

== External links ==
{{Scholia}}
Examples of software tools developed by Minor and his lab:
* [https://www.hkl-xray.com/ HKL Research] (an official site of the company that distributes HKL2000/HKL3000)
* [https://proteindiffraction.org/ proteindiffraction.org] (a public repository of diffraction images)
* [https://cmm.minorlab.org/ CMM] (a server for validation of metal-binding sites in macromolecular structures)
* [https://checkmyblob.bioreproducibility.org/server/ CheckMyBlob] (a machine learning system that automatically detects and validates ligands in X-ray electron density maps)
* [https://molstack.bioreproducibility.org/ Molstack] (an online platform for sharing electron density maps and their interpretations)
* [https://fitmunk.bioreproducibility.org/ Fitmunk] (a server for a framework for fitting side-chain conformations on a fixed backbone into electron density)
* [https://csgid.org/metalnas/ MgRNA] (a server for classification of Mg binding sites in RNA crystal structures)
* [http://2hadh.bioreproducibility.org/ 2HADH Knowledgebase] (a server for 2HADH enzymes classification and structural and enzymatic data)
* [https://labdb.minorlab.org/labdb LabDB] (an instance of a laboratory information management system for structural biology)
* [https://covid-19.bioreproducibility.org/ Validated SARS-CoV-2 related structural models] (a repository for validated SARS-CoV-2 related structural models of potential drug targets)
